column5: THE ONE BLOCK WAVE 60 LEFT UNCOMPARED IS COMPARED THIS PASS AND IT FOUND A DEFECT UNDER IT THAT WOULD HAVE MADE ANY EARLIER `done` FALSE. get_metadata 7806:84981 read live, whole board, then get_design_context on 7806:85230 (the artwork) and 7806:85030 (the Standard row). MEASURED, and the first one is the reason every seam earlier waves closed was being measured against the wrong column: Main container 7806:84982 is 580 wide at (94,76) and EVERY card under it opens at x=0 on 580 - Frame 345 the header, Frame 270 the Overview card, `active` the artwork, Frame 350 carrying details and attributes. The file stated `md:max-w-[580px]` AND `md:px-4`, and under border-box that 16 comes OFF the 580, so the cards drew 548. ★ The tell was not the board: every other page in this wallet already states `md:px-0` beside the same max-width (BridgeModal :886, PortfolioChart :250, PortfolioInsights :277, ReceiveModal :474, RequestPayment :1256) and NftDisplay was the lone outlier - a house convention broken in one file, which is invisible to a check that reads only the file. BUILT (df05326): md:px-0 with lg:px-4 so lg keeps the 16 it shipped. THREE MORE OFF THE SAME READ. (1) Frame 345 is 580x28 - a 24 icons/action at y=2, a 10 gap, the 28-tall name - and Frame 270 opens at y=44, so the seam is 16; the file drew `mb-4 md:mb-6`, i.e. 24 at md, now `mb-4 lg:mb-6`. (2) 7806:85232 hangs the 20 chain badge at (24,536) on the 580 artwork: 24 from the left and 580-(536+20)=24 from the foot. (3) 7806:85234 is the 32 expand box at (524,24): 24 from the top and 580-(524+32)=24 from the right, its 24 mark at (4,4), and its plate is Green Coal 200 #122524 rather than a scrim. BOTH INSETS ARE TWICE THE PHONE'S 12 (7882:18026, 7882:18028), so the pair is stated at md with lg restored to 12 - the boards disagree about the inset, not just the size, which is exactly the shape wave 60 met on the chart nav's control placement. ★★★ THEN THE DEFECT THAT WOULD HAVE SUNK THE ROW, found only because the `done` claim was being checked line by line rather than assumed from the three fixes above: `DetailRow`'s value and the attributes grid's value were both `text-xs md:text-sm` and NOTHING ELSE, so at md they carried Tailwind's own 20px leading against rows the board draws at 16 (7806:85043 and its three siblings are 556x16; 7806:85034 is Mulish Regular 14/16). That is FOUR PER ROW - six detail rows and the six of the taller attributes column - so the details card would have closed at ~349 against its drawn 333 and the attributes card at ~263 against 239, and wave 60's freshly built 32 pitch would have rendered 36. This is the THIRD time this file has carried the same framework defect (the Overview heading in wave 59, both card headings in wave 60), and each time it was a size utility setting a box no number in the source names. BUILT (0a25b9a): md:leading-4 on both values with lg:leading-5 restoring the 20. THE ONE ELEMENT THE BOARD DRAWS THAT IS NOT DRAWN, stated rather than quietly dropped: 7806:85033 is an 18 images/circle 6 before the ERC-721 value, and read at full resolution it is the same blue disc the artwork's chain badge draws, dropped beside a TOKEN-STANDARD label. No ERC-721 art exists in this wallet and NFTItem names no source for one, and drawing the chain's mark there would say the standard is a chain - the label-is-the-fabrication shape. So the MARK stays undrawn and its BOX is held at the board's 18 (md:min-h-[18px]), which is what keeps Frame 277's 194 whole; without it the card closes at 331 against 333. Casey call, one line: draw the chain mark beside the standard, or leave the slot empty as shipped. THE 768 COLUMN NOW MATCHES END TO END: 580 at (94,76); header 28 + 16; Overview 12+19+16+48+24+50+12 = 181; 8; artwork 580x580 r12 with the badge and expand box both inset 24; 8; details 12+19+20+56+20+194+12 = 333; 8; attributes 12+19+20+176+12 = 239. Frame 347 Your activity is 738 wide on a 580 board and hidden, so it is correctly undrawn. 375 and 1440 are n-a for THIS key - it is a 768x1024 board, its phone twins are 7882-18863 and 7882-17627 with their own rows, and every change above is gated at md with lg explicitly restored. Second witness modules/skai-wallet/src/components/NftDisplay.tabletColumn.test.tsx; mount site modules/skai-wallet/src/pages/wallet/WalletNftDetailRoute.tsx via NftDetailModal. Commits df05326, 0a25b9a (modules/skai-wallet). tsc --noEmit in modules/skai-wallet exit 0, --listFilesOnly confirmed it read both edited files. 60 tests green across the seven NftDisplay suites. ★ THE FIVE NEW CASES WERE PROVED TO BITE: with all four values reverted in the working tree, exactly five failed naming the reverted numbers, and the file was restored from df05326. Not deployed. No browser: source-vs-node.

HAND-OFF FROM wallet-shell-pages, TAKEN BECAUSE THE FILE IS THIS LANE'S - AND THE PRESCRIBED CHANGE WAS REFUSED ON ARITHMETIC AND REPLACED. ⛔ THIS LANE OPENED NONE OF THE THREE BOARDS (7727-14937, 7727-14974, 7727-15382); the block's numbers are that lane's measurement, and the VERDICT on the three frames is theirs to write. What is certified here is the arithmetic and the build. THE HAND-OFF: the patterns block draws 715.5x283.27 at (-103,564) on the 375 board, and the fix given was to write those four numbers onto the inner svg. CHECKED FIRST, as that lane asked: 283.27/659.954 = 0.429227 against 715.5/1665.35 = 0.429645, a delta of 0.0004, which on a 715 box is 0.3px - so the aspect agrees and the board is not being read in a different space. THE FOUR NUMBERS ARE STILL WRONG THERE, and this is the finding. WelcomeDecor is `xMidYMax slice` over a 1440x900 viewBox filling the viewport, so at 375x812 it scales by max(375/1440,812/900) = 0.9022 and CUTS (1440*0.9022 - 375)/2 = 462 of user space off EACH SIDE: only user x 512 to 928 is ever on screen. x="-103" width="715.5" in that space lands at device x -555.0 to 90.5 and 645.5 wide - almost entirely off the left edge, and the wrong size - against a board wanting -103.0 to 612.5 at 715.5. ★ And the cut is a FUNCTION OF THE VIEWPORT WIDTH, so no static set of attributes inside that svg is right at two widths; the ratio check the hand-off proposed cannot catch this, because aspect is preserved either way. The tell was structural, one ancestor's coordinate space, exactly the trap the wave rules name. BUILT INSTEAD (5c51e3b): the rung is set on the CANVAS BOX, not on the art. The scale the board asks for is 715.5/1665.35 = 0.42964, so the canvas wants to be 1440 and 900 AT that scale - 618.68x386.68 - with its left edge at -45.00 and its foot 7.83 above the container's; as ratios of its own box that is w-[164.982%] of the container with translate-x-[-7.273%] and translate-y-[-2.025%], anchored bottom-left on aspect-[1440/900], all restored at md (md:inset-0 md:h-full md:w-full md:aspect-auto md:translate-x-0 md:translate-y-0). Recomputed through the whole chain that yields the block at -103.00, 564.00, 715.50x283.54 against a drawn 283.27 - the quarter-pixel is the board's own rounding, the same 0.0004 as above. Nothing is stretched: the box keeps the canvas's 1440:900. ★★★ A FIRST ATTEMPT WAS THROWN AWAY AND THE REASON IS WORTH CARRYING: it gave the art a second svg positioned against the viewport, which put TWO copies of the paths in the DOM and broke a sibling lane's standing assertion in WalletShellWelcome.figmaDesktop.test.tsx (`.wb-globe` counted 6 against a drawn 3). Moving the CANVAS works only because that svg carries nothing but the patterns - checked, its children are one `style` element and the one nested svg - so there is no duplication and 1440 and 768 are untouched. A peer's failing test was the thing that found it. MUTATION-CHECKED BOTH WAYS, as that lane asked: reverted to the single full-viewport rung, 3 of 5 cases fail; and with the literal hand-off applied (the board's four numbers on the inner svg, canvas restored), 3 of 5 fail again, one of them the case that pins the art's own x/y/width/height. File restored from 5c51e3b both times. Second witness modules/skai-wallet/src/components/wallet/welcome/WelcomeBackground.phonePatterns.test.tsx; mount site modules/skai-wallet/src/pages/wallet/WalletShellWelcome.tsx.
